claim: NfsA is a member of a large bacterial superfamily comprising highly promiscuous FMN-dependent oxidoreductases that accept electrons from NAD(P)H and transfer them to a diverse range of substrates.
source: NfsA is a member of a large bacterial superfamily comprising highly promiscuous FMN-dependent oxidoreductases that accept electrons from NAD(P)H and transfer them to a diverse range of substrates (Williams et al., 2015; Akiva et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Williams et al., 2015 and Akiva et al., 2017.

claim: Expression of nfsA is governed by the soxRS regulon.
source: Expression of nfsA is governed by the soxRS regulon, and NfsA is thought to guard against oxidative stress through reduction of water-soluble quinones such as 1,4-benzoquinone (Liochev et al., 1999; Paterson et al., 2002; Copp et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Liochev et al., 1999, Paterson et al., 2002, and Copp et al., 2017.

claim: NfsA is thought to guard against oxidative stress through reduction of water-soluble quinones such as 1,4-benzoquinone.
source: Expression of nfsA is governed by the soxRS regulon, and NfsA is thought to guard against oxidative stress through reduction of water-soluble quinones such as 1,4-benzoquinone (Liochev et al., 1999; Paterson et al., 2002; Copp et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Liochev et al., 1999, Paterson et al., 2002, and Copp et al., 2017.

claim: NfsA is able to reduce a wide diversity of nitroaromatic compounds.
source: Although most efficient with quinone substrates, NfsA is also able to reduce a wide diversity of nitroaromatic compounds (Valiauga et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Valiauga et al., 2017.

claim: There are relatively few nitroaromatic natural products.
source: This is generally believed to represent non-physiological substrate ambiguity, as there are relatively few nitroaromatic natural products, and in many cases nitro-reduction yields a more toxic derivative (Winkler and Hertweck, 2007; Parry et al., 2011; Williams et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Winkler and Hertweck, 2007, Parry et al., 2011, and Williams et al., 2015.

claim: In many cases nitro-reduction yields a more toxic derivative.
source: This is generally believed to represent non-physiological substrate ambiguity, as there are relatively few nitroaromatic natural products, and in many cases nitro-reduction yields a more toxic derivative (Winkler and Hertweck, 2007; Parry et al., 2011; Williams et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Winkler and Hertweck, 2007, Parry et al., 2011, and Williams et al., 2015.

claim: Nitro-reduction of chloramphenicol transforms this antibiotic to a product that is not discernibly toxic to bacteria.
source: An important exception is that nitro-reduction of chloramphenicol transforms this antibiotic to a product that is not discernibly toxic to bacteria (Yunis, 1988; Erwin et al., 2007; Crofts et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Yunis, 1988, Erwin et al., 2007, and Crofts et al., 2019.

claim: Over-expressed native NfsA confers only slight chloramphenicol protection to E. coli host cells.
source: We have observed that over-expressed native NfsA confers only slight chloramphenicol protection to E. coli host cells, but reasoned that we could select for improved detoxification in an extremely high-throughput manner by plating variant libraries on chloramphenicol-amended media.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' own observations.

claim: Members of the bacterial nitroreductase superfamily appear to have unusually plastic active sites.
source: Because members of the bacterial nitroreductase superfamily appear to have unusually plastic active sites (Akiva et al., 2017), we considered that simultaneous mass-mutagenesis of up to eight active-site residues should be possible.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Akiva et al., 2017.

claim: The degenerate gene library represented 430 million possible gene combinations, collectively specifying 394 million different NfsA variants.
source: In total, our library represented 430 million possible gene combinations, collectively specifying 394 million different NfsA variants.
evidence: The claim is based on the design of the degenerate gene library described in the manuscript.

claim: A total of 398 million transformed colonies were recovered, representing 252 million different NfsA variants.
source: We ultimately recovered a total of 398 million transformed colonies, a collection predicted by GLUE (Firth and Patrick, 2008) to represent 252 million different NfsA variants.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data and computational prediction using GLUE.

claim: Approximately 0.05% of the gene variants (~200,000 clones) were more effective than wild-type nfsA at enabling colony formation on LB agar amended with 3 µM chloramphenicol.
source: Despite the drastic reconfiguration of their encoded active sites, a surprising 0.05% of the gene variants (~200,000 clones) were more effective than wild-type nfsA (i.e. enabled colony formation on LB agar amended with 3 µM chloramphenicol, the lowest concentration at which wild-type nfsA was unable to support host cell growth).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental selection data.

claim: 30 top variants exhibited evidence of a conserved genetic response to the chloramphenicol selection.
source: Sequencing and elimination of duplicates yielded 30 top variants that exhibited evidence of a conserved genetic response to the chloramphenicol selection.
evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data of selected variants.

claim: In the top 30 variants, the native serine or threonine at positions 41 and 219 was substituted by an aromatic residue in ≥26 of the 30 cases.
source: Particularly strong trends were observed at positions 41 and 219 (where the native serine or threonine was substituted by an aromatic residue in ≥26 of the 30 cases), and at position 225 (100% substitution of the native arginine by an uncharged or acidic residue) (Figure 1C, Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data of the top 30 variants and is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: At position 225, 100% of the top 30 variants had substitution of the native arginine by an uncharged or acidic residue.
source: Particularly strong trends were observed at positions 41 and 219 (where the native serine or threonine was substituted by an aromatic residue in ≥26 of the 30 cases), and at position 225 (100% substitution of the native arginine by an uncharged or acidic residue) (Figure 1C, Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data of the top 30 variants and is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: 7NT cells expressing the 30 top variants demonstrated nearly 6- to 10-fold greater chloramphenicol tolerance than those expressing native nfsA.
source: In EC50 assays, 7NT cells expressing these 30 variants demonstrated nearly 6- to 10-fold greater chloramphenicol tolerance than those expressing native nfsA (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is based on EC50 assay data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: There was no substantial variation in expression between the top 30 variants and native nfsA.
source: SDS-PAGE analysis revealed that there was no substantial variation in expression between these variants and native nfsA, and hence the enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification was not a consequence of elevated expression levels (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on SDS-PAGE analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification was not a consequence of elevated expression levels.
source: SDS-PAGE analysis revealed that there was no substantial variation in expression between these variants and native nfsA, and hence the enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification was not a consequence of elevated expression levels (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is inferred from SDS-PAGE data showing similar expression levels.

claim: The top five chloramphenicol-detoxifying NfsA variants exhibited only marginal (at most 2.2-fold) improvements in chloramphenicol kcat/KM over wild-type NfsA.
source: We were surprised to discover that these variants exhibited only marginal (at most 2.2-fold) improvements in chloramphenicol kcat/KM over wild-type NfsA (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is based on steady-state kinetics assay data shown in Table 1.

claim: The top five variants were impaired in kcat (6–10-fold lower than NfsA) but greatly improved in KM (8–13-fold lower than NfsA).
source: However, in every case the variants were impaired in kcat (6–10-fold lower than NfsA) but greatly improved in KM (8–13-fold lower than NfsA).
evidence: The claim is based on kinetic parameters measured in steady-state kinetics assays.

claim: The in vivo improvements in chloramphenicol detoxification were driven primarily by enhanced substrate affinity.
source: Thus, it appeared that the in vivo improvements in chloramphenicol detoxification were driven primarily by enhanced substrate affinity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the kinetic data showing improved KM but decreased kcat.

claim: 1,4-benzoquinone reduction was unmeasurable in each of the five top chloramphenicol-detoxifying variants.
source: However, when assayed individually we found that 1,4-benzoquinone reduction was unmeasurable in each of the five top chloramphenicol-detoxifying variants (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is based on enzyme activity assay data shown in Table 1.

claim: For wild-type NfsA, 1,4-benzoquinone reduction (kcat/KM = 5.8 × 10^6) is nearly 1000-fold more efficient than chloramphenicol reduction.
source: In contrast, for wild-type NfsA, 1,4-benzoquinone reduction (kcat/KM = 5.8 × 106; Valiauga et al., 2017) is nearly 1000-fold more efficient than chloramphenicol reduction (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is based on kinetic data from Table 1 and a citation to Valiauga et al., 2017.

claim: The data are consistent with in vivo chloramphenicol reduction having been amplified for the selected variants by the elimination of competitive quinone inhibition.
source: Our data are therefore consistent with in vivo chloramphenicol reduction having been amplified for the selected variants by the elimination of competitive quinone inhibition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the kinetic data showing loss of quinone activity and improved chloramphenicol activity.

claim: Variant 36_37 has seven substitutions: S41Y, H215C, T219Y, K222V, S224R, R225V, F227G.
source: The top two chloramphenicol-detoxifying variants (on the basis of EC50 measurements; 36_37 and 20_39) each had seven substitutions at the eight targeted positions, with both containing the wild-type residue leucine at position 43 (36_37 = S41Y, H215C, T219Y, K222V, S224R, R225V, F227G; 20_39 = S41Y, H215N, T219Y, K222R, S224Y, R225D, F227H; Figure 2A–C).
evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data and structural models shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Variant 20_39 has seven substitutions: S41Y, H215N, T219Y, K222R, S224Y, R225D, F227H.
source: The top two chloramphenicol-detoxifying variants (on the basis of EC50 measurements; 36_37 and 20_39) each had seven substitutions at the eight targeted positions, with both containing the wild-type residue leucine at position 43 (36_37 = S41Y, H215C, T219Y, K222V, S224R, R225V, F227G; 20_39 = S41Y, H215N, T219Y, K222R, S224Y, R225D, F227H; Figure 2A–C).
evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data and structural models shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: There are 126 possible intermediate forms between wild-type NfsA and each selected variant.
source: Therefore, there are 126 possible intermediate forms (27 – 2) between wild-type NfsA and each selected variant.
evidence: The claim is based on mathematical calculation of possible combinations.

claim: There was no clear path from NfsA to either variant 36_37 or 20_39 that involved exclusively upward steps in the hypothetical evolutionary trajectory.
source: In neither case was there a clear path from NfsA to the final variant that involved exclusively upward steps in the hypothetical evolutionary trajectory (Figure 2D–F).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of all intermediate variants shown in Figure 2D-F.

claim: The final two substitutions (H215C and K222V for variant 36_37, and K222R and S224Y for variant 20_39) did not contribute substantially to the overall chloramphenicol-detoxifying activity of each variant.
source: Nevertheless, it was evident that the final two substitutions (H215C and K222V for variant 36_37, and K222R and S224Y for variant 20_39) did not contribute substantially to the overall chloramphenicol-detoxifying activity of each variant.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of intermediate variant activities.

claim: Iterative evolutionary strategies could have plausibly generated NfsA variants exhibiting similar levels of chloramphenicol-detoxifying activity to 36_37 and 20_39, but there were very few accessible pathways for this.
source: Thus, we concluded that iterative evolutionary strategies could have plausibly generated NfsA variants exhibiting similar levels of chloramphenicol-detoxifying activity to 36_37 and 20_39, but that there were very few accessible pathways for this (Figure 2D–E).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the evolutionary trajectory analysis shown in Figure 2D-E.

claim: Only one of the seven substitutions present in each of variants 36_37 and 20_39 significantly enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification when introduced on an individual basis.
source: Most prominently, we noted that only one of the seven substitutions present in each of variants 36_37 and 20_39 significantly enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification when introduced on an individual basis (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The single substitution that significantly enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification was at residue R225 in both variants.
source: Although it was the same residue, R225, that was substituted in each case, the substituting residues possessed very different chemical properties (negatively charged aspartate in 20_39 versus non-polar valine in 36_37).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data and analysis of individual substitutions.

claim: None of the top 30 selected variants had retained an arginine at position 225.
source: This, together with the observation that none of our top 30 selected variants had retained an arginine at position 225 (Figure 1C, Supplementary file 1a), suggested that it was important for arginine 225 to be eliminated before the other active-site substitutions could make a discernible contribution to improved chloramphenicol detoxification.
evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data shown in Figure 1C and Supplementary file 1a.

claim: It was important for arginine 225 to be eliminated before the other active-site substitutions could make a discernible contribution to improved chloramphenicol detoxification.
source: This, together with the observation that none of our top 30 selected variants had retained an arginine at position 225 (Figure 1C, Supplementary file 1a), suggested that it was important for arginine 225 to be eliminated before the other active-site substitutions could make a discernible contribution to improved chloramphenicol detoxification.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that all top variants lack R225 and individual substitution data.

claim: S41Y and T219Y did not confer a significant improvement in chloramphenicol detoxification when introduced to NfsA individually or together.
source: For example, both of the top selected variants contained the substitutions S41Y and T219Y, neither of which conferred a significant improvement in chloramphenicol detoxification when introduced to NfsA individually (Figure 3A) or together (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: When S41Y was introduced into an R225V or R225D background, it yielded a significant increase in chloramphenicol detoxification.
source: When each was introduced into an R225V or R225D background, S41Y yielded a significant increase in chloramphenicol detoxification, but T219Y did not (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The combination of S41Y and T219Y together with R225V or R225D gave a further significant improvement in chloramphenicol detoxification.
source: However, the combination of S41Y and T219Y together with R225V or R225D gave a further significant improvement (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Complex epistatic interactions render >99% of the 5040 hypothetical evolutionary pathways broadly inaccessible to iterative mutagenesis strategies.
source: Overall, our data suggest that complex epistatic interactions render >99% of the 5040 hypothetical evolutionary pathways (that might be traversed from wild-type NfsA to either 36_37 or 20_39) broadly inaccessible to iterative mutagenesis strategies.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the analysis of all evolutionary trajectories and epistatic interactions.

claim: The first substitution of both hypothetical trajectories (i.e. the elimination of R225) was sufficient to abolish nearly all 1,4-benzoquinone activity.
source: From these data, it was evident that the first substitution of both hypothetical trajectories (i.e. the elimination of R225) was sufficient to abolish nearly all 1,4-benzoquinone activity.
evidence: The claim is based on kinetic assay data of intermediate variants.

claim: R225 plays a key role in binding 1,4-benzoquinone substrate.
source: A structure of NfsA with 1,4-benzoquinone in the active site was reported from the Hyde group that proposes the quinone is held in place through interactions between one of its carbonyl oxygens and the backbone of S41, while the other carbonyl oxygen interacts with the guanidinium of R225 and/or the amine of Q67 (Day, 2013). Our data are consistent with R225 playing a key role in binding this substrate.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Day, 2013 and is consistent with the authors' experimental data.

claim: The level of 1,4-benzoquinone activity remained unmeasurably low with all subsequent substitutions after R225 elimination.
source: The level of 1,4-benzoquinone activity remained unmeasurably low with all subsequent substitutions (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: The claim is based on kinetic assay data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: The sustained loss of 1,4-benzoquinone activity throughout each trajectory is consistent with elimination of quinone competition promoting more effective chloramphenicol reduction.
source: The sustained loss of 1,4-benzoquinone activity throughout each trajectory is consistent with elimination of quinone competition promoting more effective chloramphenicol reduction.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the kinetic data showing loss of quinone activity and improved chloramphenicol activity.

claim: Variants that retained R225 were on average no better than wild-type NfsA at defending host cells against chloramphenicol (mean fold improvement of 1.0 ± 0.5).
source: The variants that retained R225 were on average no better than wild-type NfsA at defending host cells against chloramphenicol (mean fold improvement of 1.0 ± 0.5), while cells expressing variants that contained the substitution R225V or R225D were on average able to tolerate 4.0 ± 2.4 fold higher chloramphenicol concentrations than those expressing wild-type nfsA (Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of all intermediate variants shown in Supplementary file 1c.

claim: Cells expressing variants that contained the substitution R225V or R225D were on average able to tolerate 4.0 ± 2.4 fold higher chloramphenicol concentrations than those expressing wild-type nfsA.
source: The variants that retained R225 were on average no better than wild-type NfsA at defending host cells against chloramphenicol (mean fold improvement of 1.0 ± 0.5), while cells expressing variants that contained the substitution R225V or R225D were on average able to tolerate 4.0 ± 2.4 fold higher chloramphenicol concentrations than those expressing wild-type nfsA (Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of all intermediate variants shown in Supplementary file 1c.

claim: The substitution S41Y yielded a profound improvement in chloramphenicol KM, but also diminished kcat substantially.
source: The substitution S41Y that came next in both trajectories yielded a profound improvement in chloramphenicol KM, but also diminished kcat substantially (Figure 4B and C and Figure 4F and G).
evidence: The claim is based on kinetic data shown in Figure 4B, C, F, and G.

claim: S41Y most likely enables planar stabilisation and stacking of nitroaromatic substrates between the isoalloxazine rings of flavin mononucleotide (FMN) and the introduced tyrosine.
source: We observed the same S41Y NfsA substitution in our previous PR-104A study, and concluded that this most likely enables planar stabilisation and stacking of nitroaromatic substrates between the isoalloxazine rings of flavin mononucleotide (FMN) and the introduced tyrosine (Copp et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on a previous study by the authors (Copp et al., 2017) and inference from structural considerations.

claim: The improved affinity for chloramphenicol is likely explained by planar stabilisation and stacking between FMN and the introduced tyrosine, with the decrease in catalytic turnover arising as a consequence of enhanced stabilisation of the Michaelis complex.
source: It is likely that a similar phenomenon explains the improved affinity for chloramphenicol observed here, with the decrease in catalytic turnover also arising as a consequence of enhanced stabilisation of the Michaelis complex.
evidence: The claim is inferred from kinetic data and structural considerations.

claim: The subsequent substitutions after S41Y act to 'tune' the system, exerting only minor effects on kcat, but overall yielding incremental improvements in chloramphenicol KM.
source: The subsequent substitutions in each trajectory then act to 'tune' the system, exerting only minor effects on kcat, but overall yielding incremental improvements in chloramphenicol KM that largely mirror the improved chloramphenicol detoxification observed in vivo (Figure 4C and E and Figure 4D and F).
evidence: The claim is based on kinetic data shown in Figure 4C, D, E, and F.

claim: The expression levels were consistent for each intermediate variant throughout the hypothetical evolutionary progression.
source: SDS-PAGE analysis confirmed that the expression levels were consistent for each intermediate variant throughout the hypothetical evolutionary progression, eliminating this as a variable exerting substantial influence on the relative activity levels in vivo (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is based on SDS-PAGE analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Using epPCR to introduce mutations across the entire nfsA coding sequence, 50 unique sequences were identified, each of which encoded a protein that was substituted at the R225 position.
source: When each gene variant was sequenced, it was revealed that there were 50 unique sequences, each of which encoded a protein that was substituted at the R225 position (Supplementary file 1e).
evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data of epPCR-selected variants shown in Supplementary file 1e.

claim: Sequencing of 20 randomly-chosen clones grown without chloramphenicol selection identified no R225 substitutions, confirming that the epPCR library was not profoundly biased towards mutation of codon 225.
source: In contrast, sequencing of 20 randomly-chosen clones grown without chloramphenicol selection identified no R225 substitutions, confirming that the epPCR library was not profoundly biased towards mutation of codon 225 (Supplementary file 1f).
evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data of unselected clones shown in Supplementary file 1f.

claim: Codon 225 was mutated exclusively at the first nucleotide position, giving substitutions R225C (C→T, 47 times), R225S (C→A, seven times) or R225G (C→G, six times).
source: We were surprised to note (Supplementary file 1e) that codon 225 was mutated exclusively at the first nucleotide position, giving substitutions R225C (C→T, 47 times), R225S (C→A, seven times) or R225G (C→G, six times), but not at the second nucleotide position (which would have given rise to R225L/P/H).
evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data shown in Supplementary file 1e.

claim: 100% of epPCR-selected variants were mutated at codon 225.
source: Irrespective, that 100% of selected variants were mutated at codon 225 provides compelling evidence that eliminating quinone competition is a key first step towards evolving improved chloramphenicol detoxification, and that substitution of R225 is the most attainable way to achieve this.
evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data of epPCR-selected variants.

claim: Eliminating quinone competition is a key first step towards evolving improved chloramphenicol detoxification.
source: Irrespective, that 100% of selected variants were mutated at codon 225 provides compelling evidence that eliminating quinone competition is a key first step towards evolving improved chloramphenicol detoxification, and that substitution of R225 is the most attainable way to achieve this.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that all selected variants have R225 substitutions and the loss of quinone activity.

claim: Substitution of R225 is the most attainable way to eliminate quinone competition.
source: Irrespective, that 100% of selected variants were mutated at codon 225 provides compelling evidence that eliminating quinone competition is a key first step towards evolving improved chloramphenicol detoxification, and that substitution of R225 is the most attainable way to achieve this.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that all selected variants have R225 substitutions.

claim: For four of the five prodrugs tested, host sensitivity was largely unchanged (EC50 within a range of 0.8 to 2-fold that of the NfsA-expressing strain) when expressing any of the variants.
source: However, for four of the five prodrugs, host sensitivity was largely unchanged (EC50 within a range of 0.8 to 2-fold that of the NfsA-expressing strain) when expressing any of the variants (Figure 5C–F).
evidence: The claim is based on EC50 assay data shown in Figure 5C-F.

claim: All variants exhibited similar gains in metronidazole activity to chloramphenicol, despite the two compounds sharing little structural similarity.
source: The exception was metronidazole, for which all variants exhibited similar gains in activity to chloramphenicol, despite the two compounds sharing little structural similarity (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: The claim is based on EC50 assay data shown in Figure 5A-B.

claim: The introduction of R225V or R225D substitutions into NfsA significantly enhanced activity with metronidazole and CB1954.
source: Moreover, the introduction of R225V or R225D substitutions into NfsA (which largely eliminate 1,4-benzoquinone activity; Figure 4A–B) did not improve reduction of all prodrugs, but only significantly enhanced activity with metronidazole and CB1954 (Student's t-test; Figure 5B,D).
evidence: The claim is based on EC50 assay data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 5B and D.

claim: Selection for enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification was not driven exclusively by loss of the competing quinone activity.
source: We therefore concluded that our selection for enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification was not driven exclusively by loss of the competing quinone activity, as this would have tended to also enhance activity with other alternate substrates.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that not all prodrug activities were enhanced.

claim: Metronidazole is cheap, widely-available, and has no measurable bystander effect in E. coli.
source: Because metronidazole is cheap, widely-available, and has no measurable bystander effect in E. coli (i.e. unlike many other nitroaromatic prodrugs its toxic metabolites are confined solely to the activating cell [Chan-Hyams et al., 2018]), we considered it ideally suited for counter-selection applications.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Chan-Hyams et al., 2018.

claim: Chloramphenicol maintained plasmids bearing either 36_37 or 20_39 in E. coli 7NT in 100% of cases (94/94 colonies tested).
source: The resulting colonies were then tested for retention or loss of the plasmid, respectively, with the expected outcome being realised in 100% of cases (94/94 colonies tested; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Metronidazole forced elimination of plasmids bearing either 36_37 or 20_39 in E. coli 7NT in 100% of cases (94/94 colonies tested).
source: The resulting colonies were then tested for retention or loss of the plasmid, respectively, with the expected outcome being realised in 100% of cases (94/94 colonies tested; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The selected variants might have useful applications as dual selectable/counter-selectable marker genes.
source: This suggests that our selected variants might indeed have useful applications as dual selectable/counter-selectable marker genes.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the observed selection and counter-selection properties.

claim: The reconstructed NfsA 'engine' is unlikely to be an optimal fit within the pre-existing chassis.
source: We acknowledge that this approach of focusing exclusively on eight key active-site residues means the reconstructed NfsA 'engine' is unlikely to be an optimal fit within the pre-existing chassis, and that further gains in activity would undoubtedly result by selecting residue substitutions in the second shell, or beyond.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning by the authors about the limitations of their approach.

claim: Further gains in activity would undoubtedly result by selecting residue substitutions in the second shell, or beyond.
source: We acknowledge that this approach of focusing exclusively on eight key active-site residues means the reconstructed NfsA 'engine' is unlikely to be an optimal fit within the pre-existing chassis, and that further gains in activity would undoubtedly result by selecting residue substitutions in the second shell, or beyond.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning by the authors about potential improvements.

claim: Error-prone PCR can only access a limited and unbalanced repertoire of residues (on average, only 5.7 of the 19 alternative amino acids per codon position, with a bias towards similar residues).
source: Nevertheless, we reasoned that our approach would allow us to gain comprehensive insight into key catalytic changes driving improved chloramphenicol detoxification, without being subject to the stochastic vagaries of epPCR, or the well-established phenomenon that it can only access a limited and unbalanced repertoire of residues (on average, only 5.7 of the 19 alternative amino acids per codon position, with a bias towards similar residues [Hermes et al., 1990]).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hermes et al., 1990.

claim: The strong trade-off between quinone and chloramphenicol reduction is a very different scenario to the predominantly weak trade-offs observed in previous laboratory evolution studies.
source: The strong trade-off between quinone and chloramphenicol reduction is a very different scenario to the predominantly weak trade-offs observed in previous laboratory evolution studies (e.g. those reviewed by Kaltenbach et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim compares the current findings to previous studies reviewed by Kaltenbach et al., 2016.

claim: Ben-David et al., 2020 encountered an abrupt activity trade-off when they evolved the calcium-dependent lactonase mammalian paraoxonase-1 into an efficient organophosphate hydrolase.
source: Even the more recent work of Ben-David et al., 2020 who encountered an abrupt activity trade-off when they evolved the calcium-dependent lactonase mammalian paraoxonase-1 into an efficient organophosphate hydrolase, found that the native functionality could subsequently be restored and was not incompatible with the evolved one (Ben-David et al., 2013; Ben-David et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ben-David et al., 2013 and Ben-David et al., 2020.

claim: In the Ben-David et al. study, the native functionality could subsequently be restored and was not incompatible with the evolved one.
source: Even the more recent work of Ben-David et al., 2020 who encountered an abrupt activity trade-off when they evolved the calcium-dependent lactonase mammalian paraoxonase-1 into an efficient organophosphate hydrolase, found that the native functionality could subsequently be restored and was not incompatible with the evolved one (Ben-David et al., 2013; Ben-David et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ben-David et al., 2013 and Ben-David et al., 2020.

claim: Most previous laboratory evolution studies have evaded the phenomenon of active selection against the original function by focusing on heterologous enzymes and/or exogenously applied substrates.
source: Together, these examples support the proposal of Kaltenbach et al., 2016 that during natural evolution of a promiscuous activity there is likely to be active selection against the original function, as well as our own supposition that most previous laboratory evolution studies have evaded this phenomenon by focusing on heterologous enzymes and/or exogenously applied substrates.
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparison with previous studies and supported by citation to Kaltenbach et al., 2016.

claim: During natural evolution of a promiscuous activity there is likely to be active selection against the original function.
source: Together, these examples support the proposal of Kaltenbach et al., 2016 that during natural evolution of a promiscuous activity there is likely to be active selection against the original function, as well as our own supposition that most previous laboratory evolution studies have evaded this phenomenon by focusing on heterologous enzymes and/or exogenously applied substrates.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Kaltenbach et al., 2016 and the authors' data.

claim: Positive selection alone does not lead to specialisation.
source: Moreover, our observations that the unselected promiscuous activities of NfsA (reduction of a structurally diverse panel of prodrugs) were mostly unaffected is consistent with their central thesis, that positive selection alone does not lead to specialisation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the authors' data and is consistent with a thesis from previous work.

claim: Evolution in the natural intracellular milieu involves both selection for the new function, and selection against the old.
source: The emerging picture is that evolution in the natural intracellular milieu involves both selection for the new function, and selection against the old.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the authors' findings and discussion of previous work.

claim: NfsA is less essential to the fitness of its host cell than ProA.
source: An interesting difference between our scenario and that of the Copley team is that NfsA is less essential to the fitness of its host cell than ProA (e.g. deletion of nfsA does not impair E. coli growth even under oxidative stress from heavy metal challenge [Ackerley et al., 2004]).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ackerley et al., 2004.

claim: When a new stress is encountered and a promiscuous function becomes essential, NfsA can potentially evolve without necessitating gene duplication to preserve the original function.
source: This means that when a new stress is encountered and a promiscuous function becomes essential, as we have modelled here, the enzyme can potentially evolve without necessitating gene duplication to preserve the original function.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that NfsA is not essential and can evolve new functions.

claim: The nitroreductase superfamily that NfsA belongs to spans activities as divergent as quinone reduction, flavin reduction to power bioluminescence, flavin fragmentation, dehalogenation and dehydrogenation.
source: An apparent 'freedom to operate' is manifest in the vast diversity of primary functionalities observed in the superfamily of nitroreductases that NfsA belongs to (which spans activities as divergent as quinone reduction, flavin reduction to power bioluminescence, flavin fragmentation, dehalogenation and dehydrogenation [Akiva et al., 2017]).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Akiva et al., 2017.

claim: Only a minority of enzymes in a cell are under active selection for improved catalytic activity at any time.
source: Although this contrasts with the prevailing Innovation–Amplification–Divergence (IAD) model for natural enzyme evolution (Bergthorsson et al., 2007), it may not be an exceptional scenario – rather, as previously argued by Newton et al., 2015 it is likely that only a minority of enzymes in a cell are under active selection for improved catalytic activity at any time, and redundancy in metabolic networks means that there is latent evolutionary potential that can be immediately tapped to adapt to stress without the requirement of rare and costly gene duplication events.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bergthorsson et al., 2007 and Newton et al., 2015.

claim: The degenerate codon NDT specifies 12 different amino acids that represent a balanced portfolio of small and large, polar and non-polar, aliphatic and aromatic, and negatively and positively charged side chains.
source: The degenerate codon NDT was preferred at most sites, as this specifies 12 different amino acids that represent a balanced portfolio of small and large, polar and non-polar, aliphatic and aromatic, and negatively and positively charged side chains (Reetz et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Reetz et al., 2008.

claim: Many (if not all) enzymes are promiscuous.
source: Many (if not all) enzymes are promiscuous, meaning that in addition to their primary biological role(s) they can catalyse minor side reactions that have no apparent physiological relevance, either because they are too inefficient or because the substrate is not naturally encountered (Copley, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Copley, 2015.

claim: Promiscuity can play an important role in contingency, providing a reservoir of potential functions that a cell can tap in response to changing circumstances.
source: From an evolutionary perspective, promiscuity can play an important role in contingency, providing a reservoir of potential functions that a cell can tap in response to changing circumstances (O'Brien and Herschlag, 1999; Copley, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to O'Brien and Herschlag, 1999 and Copley, 2015.

claim: A strong selection pressure can cause latent promiscuous activities to be rapidly amplified to physiologically relevant levels.
source: As demonstrated by the emergence of resistance to xenobiotic pollutants or clinical antibiotics (O'Brien and Herschlag, 1999; Hall, 2004; Ramos et al., 2005; Copley, 2009; Khersonsky and Tawfik, 2010), a strong selection pressure can cause latent promiscuous activities to be rapidly amplified to physiologically relevant levels (Newton et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Laboratory evolution studies have indicated that selection for substantial increases in a promiscuous activity typically results in only weak trade-offs against the native activity.
source: These laboratory evolution studies have indicated that selection for substantial increases in a promiscuous activity typically results in only weak trade-offs against the native activity; and therefore, the transition from one primary function to another tends to progress via generalist enzyme intermediates (Kaltenbach et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kaltenbach et al., 2016.

claim: The transition from one primary function to another tends to progress via generalist enzyme intermediates.

claim: Tawfik and co-workers proposed that enzymes possess an innate 'robustness' and stability that buffers them against the potentially detrimental effects of novel mutations, coupled with a 'plasticity' that can amplify promiscuous functions with relatively few mutations.
source: In 2005, Tawfik and co-workers proposed that enzymes possess an innate 'robustness' and stability that buffers them against the potentially detrimental effects of novel mutations, coupled with a 'plasticity' that can amplify promiscuous functions with relatively few mutations (Aharoni et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Aharoni et al., 2005.

claim: Tokuriki and co-workers demonstrated that a robust native activity is not a prerequisite for weak trade-offs.
source: More recently, Tokuriki and co-workers demonstrated that a robust native activity is not a prerequisite for weak trade-offs, and suggested that the predominance of these in the literature may instead be artefactual; a consequence of laboratory evolution studies being highly biased towards strong selection for a new function without any selection against the native activity (Kaltenbach et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kaltenbach et al., 2016.

claim: The studies overviewed by the Tokuriki team were heavily biased towards heterologous enzyme expression and/or a transition in activity from one exogenously applied substrate to another.
source: In addition to their exclusive emphasis on positive selection, we note that the studies overviewed by the Tokuriki team were also heavily biased towards heterologous enzyme expression and/or a transition in activity from one exogenously applied substrate to another (Kaltenbach et al., 2016).
